Chocolate Covered Apple Slices with date caramel & chopped peanuts! 🍎🍫 This is such a fun snack to make this fall (especially for an after-school treat!) You can customize with any toppings you’d like – a peanut butter drizzle, coconut, dried fruit, crushed Oreos, sprinkles, etc. 

The basic process is to slice an apple (we use honeycrisp) about 1/4” thick, pat it dry, then insert a popsicle or cake pop stick in the bottom. (Do a trial run before you slice the whole apple, because if it’s too thin, the apple slice will split! It can also help to make a hole with something sharp like a skewer first.) 

Coat both sides in melted chocolate of your choice, then add toppings. Keep these stored in the fridge for ~3 days (after that, the apple may start to get a little mushy). Enjoy!

High Protein Chocolate Crunch Cake

@chestbrah.official actually in my f*ckin house. 😂

👨‍🍳 Ingredients, makes 2 serves

✅ Self Raising Flour, 30g (¼ cup)
✅ Dutch Chocolate Protein Powder, 30g (1 scoop)
✅ Large Egg, 1
✅ Sugar Free Maple Syrup, 120ml (½ cup), divided
✅ Cocoa Powder, 20g (4 tbsp), divided
✅ Corn Flakes, 20g (¾ cup)

✅ Optional but if you wanted to take this to the next level melt dark chocolate and maple syrup to coat the cornflakes! 

👉 Method

1. Add the flour, whey protein, egg, half the cocoa powder and 60ml (¼ cup) sugar free maple syrup to a bowl.
2. Mix until smooth and microwave for 60 seconds. Let cool for at least 20 minutes (this keeps the cornflakes crunchy)
3. In another bowl, mix enough sugar free maple syrup and cocoa powder together to make a thick paste.
4. Add the corn flakes and fold through until completely coated.
5. Spoon the chocolate crunch mixture over the cake.
6. Dig in and enjoy

items.text: Chocolate is made by harvesting, fermenting, and drying cacao beans, which are then roasted, cracked, and winnowed to separate the inner nibs. These nibs are ground into cocoa liquor, mixed with ingredients like sugar and cocoa butter, refined, conched for smoothness, and tempered before being molded into bars.

items.title: Key Steps in Chocolate Production
items.text: Harvesting and Fermenting: Cacao pods are opened to remove the beans, which are fermented for several days to develop flavor, color, and aroma. Drying and Shipping: Fermented beans are dried (often in the sun) to reduce moisture content for shipping. Roasting: The beans are roasted at around 210°F to enhance flavor and loosen the shells. Winnowing: A machine breaks the roasted beans and separates the outer shells from the valuable inner part, called the cacao nib. Grinding and Mixing: Nibs are ground into a thick liquid called cocoa liquor (or cocoa mass). Conching: The mixture is refined to reduce particle size, then "conched"—a process involving heat, aeration, and mixing—to eliminate remaining bitterness and refine the texture. Tempering and Molding: The chocolate is tempered (precisely heated and cooled) to create a stable, shiny, and crisp finish, then molded into shapes.

items.title: Common Additives
items.text: Dark Chocolate: Cocoa liquor, cocoa butter, and sugar. Milk Chocolate: Cocoa liquor, cocoa butter, sugar, and milk powder. White Chocolate: Cocoa butter, sugar, and milk powder (no cocoa solids).

items.title: What are some popular chocolate brands?

items.text: Popular chocolate brands range from widely available, consumer-favorite candy bars like Hershey's, Reese's, KitKat, and Dove to higher-end, premium options. For gourmet or high-quality chocolate, popular choices include Lindt, Ghirardelli, Valrhona, Lake Champlain, and Läderach, which are praised for their rich taste and better ingredients.
Here are some of the most popular chocolate brands categorized by type:

items.title: Top Mass-Market/Candy Brands (USA):
items.text: Hershey's : The leading brand in the US. Reese's : Famous for peanut butter cups. KitKat : Known for its wafer-and-chocolate combination. Snickers : A top-selling chocolate bar. Dove : Widely known for milk and dark chocolate bars. Cadbury : Famous for dairy milk chocolate.

items.title: Premium & Gourmet Chocolate Brands:
items.text: Lake Champlain Chocolates : Highly rated for quality, often featuring organic and fair-trade options. Lindt: Widely accessible European chocolate known for truffles and bars. Ghirardelli: Known for high-quality, intense dark chocolate and baking products. Läderach : Top-tier Swiss chocolate, highly praised for its freshness and complex flavor. Valrhona : Frequently used by professionals and considered one of the best French chocolatiers. Whittaker's : A highly regarded New Zealand brand known for its high-quality milk chocolate. Ferrero Rocher : Known for its iconic gold-foil wrapped hazelnut chocolates.

items.title: Artisan & Specialty Brands:
items.text: Chocolove : Known for its high-percentage dark chocolate bars. TCHO : A brand known for high-quality, ethically sourced chocolate. Guittard : A popular premium brand used by many pastry chefs. Amano : An artisan producer of single-origin bars.
